correctness.rationale: For k=-f'/f and v=1-exp(-fu), the chain rule yields q=fu'exp(-fu)=v'+kH(v), where H=-(1-v)log(1-v). The sign k≥0 and H''≤-1 give q at the mixed path at least the mixture of the two nonnegative densities plus the stated quadratic Jensen term. The inverse change of variable is locally absolutely continuous on each compact interval (v stays uniformly below 1 there), starts at zero, and has nonnegative derivative. Integrating q up to T<1 bounds its mass by 1+(1/e)∫k, uniformly as T tends to 1, so square-root integration is finite even for paths diverging at 1. Equality in the integral forces equality of the two densities almost everywhere by square-root strictness; the difference of the transformed paths has zero initial data and obeys the locally Lipschitz difference equation d'=-k(H(v0)-H(v1)), giving d=0 by Gronwall on each compact interval. This works even for constant f and intervals where k vanishes. The frozen numerical checker was inspected, not executed, and is not needed for the proof.
residual_risks: Does not establish existence, regularity, uniqueness among paths with singular variation, or results for profiles with f(1)=0.
